claims.text: The MEGA-RAG framework integrates multi-source evidence retrieval combining dense retrieval via FAISS, keyword-based retrieval via BM25, and biomedical knowledge graphs.
MEGA-RAG employs a cross-encoder reranker to ensure semantic relevance of retrieved evidence.
MEGA-RAG incorporates a discrepancy-aware refinement module to enhance factual accuracy.
MEGA-RAG reduces hallucination rates by over 40% compared to PubMedBERT, PubMedGPT, standalone LLMs, and standard RAG baselines.
MEGA-RAG achieves an accuracy of 0.7913 in public health application evaluations.
MEGA-RAG achieves a precision of 0.7541 in public health application evaluations.
MEGA-RAG achieves a recall of 0.8304 in public health application evaluations.
MEGA-RAG achieves an F1 score of 0.7904 in public health application evaluations.

evidence.description: The framework integrates multi-source evidence retrieval (dense retrieval via FAISS, keyword-based retrieval via BM25, and biomedical knowledge graphs)
employs a cross-encoder reranker to ensure semantic relevance
and incorporates a discrepancy-aware refinement module to further enhance factual accuracy.

Experimental evaluation demonstrates that MEGA-RAG outperforms four baseline models [PubMedBERT, PubMedGPT, standalone LLM, and LLM with standard retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)], achieving a reduction in hallucination rates by over 40%.
It also achieves the highest accuracy (0.7913)

methodologies.name: MEGA-RAG
methodologies.description: A retrieval-augmented generation framework integrating multi-source evidence retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and discrepancy-aware answer refinement to mitigate hallucinations.

limitations.text: Large language models in public health generate hallucinations—factually inaccurate or misleading outputs that can compromise clinical communication and policy decisions.
